examples.en: We ordered flatfish sashimi at a raw fish restaurant.
Flatfish has chewy, clean-tasting flesh.
Today I bought a fresh flatfish at the market.
I like sushi made with flatfish the best.
I like salmon more than flatfish.

examples.ko: 수족관 바닥에 광어가 납작하게 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: A flatfish was lying flat on the bottom of the tank.

explain: 생선 이름으로는 '넙치'도 있지만, 횟집이나 식당에서는 '광어'라고 말해요. 보통 '광어회'처럼 회로 먹는 생선으로 자주 만나요.
explain_en: The fish also has the name '넙치', but at raw fish restaurants and in daily talk people say '광어'. You most often meet it as a sashimi fish, as in '광어회'.

examples.en: I mixed a raw egg into my rice and ate it.

examples.ko: 날달걀을 먹으면 배탈이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Eating raw eggs can give you a stomachache.
Beat one raw egg into the bowl.
There are three raw eggs in the fridge.

examples.ko: 날달걀과 삶은 달걀은 돌려 보면 구별돼요.
examples.en: You can tell a raw egg from a boiled one by spinning it.
Please crack raw eggs carefully so the shell doesn't fall in.

explain: 익히지 않은 달걀은 '날달걀'이나 '생달걀'이라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '날달걀'이 더 자주 들려요. 반대말은 '삶은 달걀', '구운 달걀'처럼 조리 방법으로 말해요. '날계란'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: An uncooked egg is called '날달걀' or '생달걀', and '날달걀' is heard more in daily talk. The opposites are described by cooking method, like '삶은 달걀' (boiled egg) and '구운 달걀' (baked egg). People also say '날계란'.

examples.en: I made broth with anchovies and kelp.
Kelp gets soft when you soak it in water.
I eat fried kelp chips as a snack.
I bought dried kelp at the market.
The broth is clean-tasting because kelp went into it.

examples.ko: 삶은 다시마에 밥과 고기를 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped rice and meat in boiled kelp and ate it.

explain: 미역과 비슷하지만 다시마는 더 두껍고 넓어서 주로 국물을 낼 때 써요. 멸치와 함께 넣어 육수를 내는 게 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: It looks like 미역 but 다시마 is thicker and wider, and it is mainly used to make broth. Boiling it together with anchovies for 육수 is the most common use.

examples.en: My grandmother washed the bellflower roots clean for me.
I caught a cold, so I drank bellflower root tea.
I bought a bag of bellflower roots at the market.
The seasoned bellflower my mom made is really delicious.
Lots of purple bellflowers bloomed on the mountain.

examples.ko: 도라지는 쓴맛이 조금 나지만 몸에 좋아요.
examples.en: Bellflower root tastes a little bitter, but it is good for you.

explain: 한국에서는 꽃보다 뿌리 나물과 약재로 더 많이 알려져 있어요. 목이 아플 때 도라지 차나 도라지청을 먹는 사람이 많아요. '도라지타령'이라는 유명한 민요도 있어요.
explain_en: In Korea it is known more as a root vegetable and herbal remedy than as a flower. Many people drink 도라지 tea or eat 도라지청 for a sore throat. There is also a famous folk song called 도라지타령.

examples.en: Please squirt mustard on the hot dog.
Mustard sauce is a little spicy and tangy.
I spread a thin layer of mustard on the bread.

examples.ko: 케첩 말고 머스터드를 더 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you give me more mustard instead of ketchup?
If you don't have mustard, you can use mayonnaise.
Even a little mustard makes the taste strong.

explain: 서양식 노란 소스를 말하고, 핫도그나 샌드위치 같은 음식에 많이 써요. 한국어의 '겨자'도 mustard를 뜻하지만, 냉면이나 겨자채에 쓰는 매운 겨자를 떠올리는 경우가 많아요. 꿀을 섞은 '허니머스터드'도 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to the yellow Western-style sauce used on hot dogs and sandwiches. The Korean word '겨자' also means mustard, but it often brings to mind the hot mustard used with cold noodles or 겨자채. You will also often see 'honey mustard', called '허니머스터드'.

examples.en: My mother set out a breakfast table for me.
Kimchi stew and rolled omelet were on the breakfast table.
I cleared the breakfast table and did the dishes.
The family sits around the breakfast table and talks.
The breakfast spread was so generous that I was surprised.
I was served a lovingly prepared breakfast at my grandmother's house.

explain: '아침밥'이나 '아침 식사'보다 상 위에 음식이 차려진 모습이 떠오르는 말이에요. '아침상을 차리다', '아침상을 치우다', '아침상을 받다'처럼 써요. 같은 방식으로 '점심상', '저녁상'도 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '아침밥' or '아침 식사', this word makes you picture the table with the food laid out on it. It is used in phrases like '아침상을 차리다' (set the table), '치우다' (clear) and '받다' (be served). In the same way you can say '점심상' and '저녁상'.

examples.ko: 양송이버섯은 볶아 먹어도 구워 먹어도 맛있어요.
examples.en: Button mushrooms taste good whether stir-fried or grilled.
I tried mushroom soup for the first time.
Please cut the button mushrooms in half.
I added button mushrooms to the stew and it tasted richer.
Stir-fry the button mushrooms and onions together in a pan.
How can you tell if button mushrooms are fresh?

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '양송이'라고도 해요. 장을 볼 때나 요리 이야기를 할 때 둘 다 알아듣는 말이에요.
explain_en: In speech it is often shortened to '양송이'. Both forms are understood when shopping or talking about cooking.

examples.en: I'm on a diet, so I eat low-calorie snacks.
I ordered a low-calorie lunch box for lunch.
This salad is low-calorie but still filling.

examples.ko: 저칼로리 음식이 꼭 맛없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Low-calorie food isn't necessarily tasteless.

examples.ko: 저칼로리 식단을 시작한 지 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a month since I started a low-calorie diet.
These days I've switched my drinks to low-calorie ones too.

explain: 반대말은 '고칼로리'예요. 저지방, 저당, 무설탕처럼 식품 포장에 자주 붙는 말이에요. 저지방이라고 해서 꼭 저칼로리인 것은 아니에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '고칼로리'. It is one of those labels, like 저지방, 저당 and 무설탕, that often appear on food packaging. Low-fat does not necessarily mean low-calorie.

examples.en: In spring I went to the mountain to dig up bamboo shoots.
The stir-fried bamboo shoots are crunchy and tasty.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤 죽순이 쑥쑥 자랐어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the bamboo shoots grew rapidly.
Bamboo shoots often go into Chinese dishes.
I bought boiled bamboo shoots at the mart.
You peel bamboo shoots before cooking them.

explain: 대나무의 어린 싹을 먹는 재료예요. 비 온 뒤 죽순처럼 빨리 자란다고 해서 '우후죽순'이라는 말도 있어요. 아삭한 식감이 특징이에요.
explain_en: It is a food ingredient, the young shoot of bamboo. Because shoots grow quickly after rain, there is also the four-character expression '우후죽순'. Its crunchy texture is a key feature.

examples.ko: 피자를 먹을 때 피클이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: When eating pizza, pickles are a must.
I make cucumber pickles myself.

examples.ko: 피클은 새콤달콤해서 느끼한 음식과 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Pickles are sweet and sour, so they go well with greasy food.
Please take the pickles out of the hamburger.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 피클 한 병이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: One jar of pickles is left in the fridge.
Pickled radish always comes out at chicken restaurants.

explain: 서양식 새콤달콤한 절임이에요. 한국에서는 치킨이나 피자와 함께 나오는 하얀 '치킨무'도 피클의 한 종류로 봐요. 김치나 장아찌 같은 한국 절임은 피클이라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: It is the sweet and sour pickle of Western cooking. In Korea the white radish served with fried chicken, 치킨무, counts as a kind of pickle too. Korean pickled foods like 김치 and 장아찌 are not called 피클.

en: relieve a hangover; eat a soup or have a drink for a hangover

examples.en: At lunch I settled my stomach with a rice soup.
My stomach burned, so I wondered what to eat to settle it.
I boiled bean sprout soup to settle my stomach.
I went to a nearby rice soup place to settle my stomach.
Eating this broth makes me feel like my stomach is settling.

examples.ko: 해장해야 하니까 오늘은 매운 건 빼 주세요.
examples.en: I need to settle my stomach, so please leave out the spicy stuff today.

explain: '국밥으로 해장하다'처럼 방법을 '(으)로'로 말해요. 많이 마신 다음 날 속을 달래는 상황이라서 보통 아침이나 점심에 써요. 가볍게는 '속을 풀다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: You state the method with '(으)로', as in '국밥으로 해장하다'. It describes calming your stomach the day after heavy drinking, so it is usually used for morning or lunch. A lighter way to say it is '속을 풀다'.

en: be squishy; be mushy; be squashy; be limp

examples.en: The overripe banana is mushy.
The noodles are mushy, so they don't taste good.
It's better to throw away fruit that has gone mushy.
After soaking for so long, my fingers went wrinkly and soft.
Flip the tofu gently so it doesn't fall apart.
I caught a cold, so my body feels weak and limp.

explain: 음식에 쓰면 면이 퍼졌거나 과일이 너무 물러서 별로라는 느낌이 있어요. 반대로 식감이 좋을 때는 '쫄깃하다'나 '단단하다'를 써요.
explain_en: For food it carries a negative feel, such as noodles that have gone soft or fruit that is too ripe. For good texture, people say '쫄깃하다' (chewy) or '단단하다' (firm) instead.
